source_caption:
In Better Call Saul’s S5•E4 "Namaste" Jimmy places a lookalike (a bartender named Hollis Early) at the defense table while his actual client sits quietly in the back of the gallery among the observers. When the prosecution's star witness confidently identifies the man at the defense table as the perpetrator, Jimmy reveals the truth. By proving the witness cannot distinguish his client from a stranger, he effectively destroys the prosecution's identification evidence.

This scene is a masterclass in misdirection that proves Saul Goodman isn't just a lawyer; he’s a magician who knows that the loudest truth is often a well-crafted lie. This moment is widely cited by fans and legal commentators as a peak example of Saul's "courtroom theatrics" using legal showmanship to win cases even when the evidence is stacked against him.

Could you spot the trap before it snapped?
